findings.title: Delete decrypt-throw uses console.warn while submit/sync use console.error
findings.problem: The delete best-effort decrypt-throw path logs via console.warn whereas submit/sync log via console.error. Both are fixed strings with no secret, so this is a cosmetic inconsistency, not a defect.
findings.fix: No change required. The warn/error split is meaningful (delete is non-fatal); keep as specified or unify only if desired.

findings.title: Submit resolution precedence stated in two places (§4.1 vs §4.3)
findings.problem: §4.1 lists template-binding-first ordering for 'submit & delete'; §4.3 prepends body numberId for submit. Reconcilable but a reader could treat §4.1 as authoritative for submit.
findings.fix: Add a sentence to §4.1 noting submit additionally accepts a body numberId that takes precedence over the template binding, pointing to §4.3 as the single authoritative precedence for submit.

findings.title: Sync abort-on-first-failing-WABA safety not explicitly tied to no-partial-write guarantee
findings.problem: The design asserts sync aborts rather than importing a partial set, but does not explicitly state that no DB mutation has occurred at abort time (all dedup/update/import run after the fetch loop). The live code confirms all mutations occur after the Meta fetch, so the abort is safe.
findings.fix: Add a half-sentence: 'No local writes have occurred at this point (dedup/update/import run only after the fetch loop), so an abort leaves the DB untouched.'
